raw_text:
Independent review of r-20260926T071140367298-s17-absent-upstream-holds
base fc399416c1ee1c9146c157afb3109568cdeb9f59, head 5be23716ed8a1747734cb3f92d9c732e530cc4b3

Read from a review worktree at 6c299f6e, with the reviewed revision checked out
read-only alongside it. The reviewed run's manifest makes the dispatch
fence-evidence, not the plan section, its spec authority; the plan's own §17
landing paragraph (docs/plans/local-lane-admission-control.html:805) records the
same behaviour, so the two agree.

Measured against the reviewed revision, not against the run's report of it.

1. The id a clive worker sends is known on a fresh router with the engine down.
   imas_ambix/agent/profiles/deepseek-v4-1-flash.toml:65 sets
   `model.served_name = "deepseek-v4.1-flash"` inside the `[model]` table opened
   at line 57. `router.py:1230` `_profile_model_ids()` folds every shipped
   profile's `served_name` into the set that `_model_is_known` (router.py:1743)
   consults. Measured on a fresh RouterApp with no upstream reachable at all and
   gate wait_seconds 0.5: POST /v1/messages for "deepseek-v4.1-flash" is held and
   answers 529 overloaded_error, "router generation queue wait limit exceeded", at
   0.61 s — not 404. The profile set on that fresh process carried nine ids,
   including both "deepseek-v4.1-flash" and "deepseek-v4-flash".

2. Non-generation paths during an engine relaunch, and whether any is fatal.
   POST /v1/messages/count_tokens for the same known id answers 404
   {"error":{"message":"unknown model id: deepseek-v4.1-flash"}}; GET /v1/models
   answers 503 {"error":{"message":"no upstream catalogs are reachable"}}; an id
   no profile names answers 404 on both. The real client (claude 2.1.283, run as
   clive runs it: ANTHROPIC_MODEL=deepseek-v4.1-flash, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL at the
   router, which was the reviewed RouterApp itself behind an aiohttp ASGI host)
   issued exactly one request in the turn: POST /v1/messages?beta=true. It called
   count_tokens and /v1/models zero times, so neither status is fatal on this
   path. With the engine appearing 25 s into the turn, that single generation
   request was held (the client's own ttft_ms 24651, time_to_request_ms 90), then
   relayed when the engine appeared: exit 0, subtype success, num_turns 1, no
   retry, result "stub-completion done". The ASGI shim was controlled before use:
   it reproduced the in-process statuses for the three raw cases exactly
   (404/404/503).

3. The held request relays with the card of the owner that admitted it, clamp
   included. Engine A (max_model_len 4096, ceiling 1024) received max_tokens
   1024; with A gone the request was held; engine B (16384, ceiling 4096)
   appeared and the held request relayed with max_tokens 4096 — B's card, not
   A's. Two mutations of my own redden the probe: an identity clamp passes
   100000 through, and a clamp aimed at a foreign 4096-token card yields 1000.

A fourth measurement, not asked for but material to fit. A held request for a
model with no engine occupies the FIFO head, and while its readiness predicate
reads false the gate admits nobody, including callers for other models whose
engines are live. Measured: X (absent model) held=True, Y (served model)
admitted=False, Y's engine saw no request. The window is bounded by the gate's
wait_seconds, and before this change the absent id was refused at once, so this
is a new cross-model delay rather than a regression of an old one — but nothing
in the diff or the plan names it.

The reviewed run's own evidence was read, not just its summary: the declared gate
ran five router suites at 706919aa (50 passed, ruff exit 0), and the declared
negative control's condition is the red log's first line verbatim, followed by
the two failures it produced (2 failed of 2 selected) and the restoration. I
re-ran the router suites that reach the changed code at the reviewed head —
tests/test_agent_router.py and tests/test_agent_router_absent_upstream.py — and
they passed 10 of 10 (EXIT=0), so the gate holds at the head and not only at the
commit it was first run on.
